sampling_model.design: Exact finite E-separation oracle; no random sampling enters the identification theorem.
sampling_model.units: Fixed finite labeled vertices \(V\) and the full finite-DMG universe with directed and unordered bidirected loops.
sampling_model.treatment: No designated treatment; the target is causal structure.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: None; estimating oracle answers is downstream.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Greatest E-representatives are proved for directed graphs and conjectured for DMGs.
Legitimate mark changes connect equivalent directed MAGs.
Cyclic FCI is complete for several \(\sigma\)-features.
Integer programming gives globally optimal learning for supported criteria.
A canonical projection exists for separable graphs.

body.tldr: E-separation gives an asymmetric Markov model for cyclic path systems, but latent coordinates introduce bidirected edges and defeat the directed canonical-graph proof. On the full finite-DMG universe, where unordered bidirected pairs may be loops, unrestricted single-edge transfer yields binary-union closure, a unique greatest representative, simultaneous admissible-edge saturation, and singleton-oracle recovery of greatest and compelled edges. A precisely defined fixed mixed SCC-profile family supplies a greatest member by edgewise saturation while retaining internal bidirected loops; the open content is contextual lifted-walk replacement for SCC changes, collider activation, directed loops, bidirected loops, and first cross-SCC bidirected connections.

project_justification.gap: The 2025 source proves only the directed greatest theorem and restricted mixed saturation; no theorem covers the cited finite-DMG universe with unordered bidirected loops, SCC-merging arrows, or first cross-SCC bidirected connections.
project_justification.niche: Latent cyclic path-space discovery lacks a canonical E-equivalence representative and a formally specified mixed SCC-profile saturation on that full edge universe.
project_justification.fill: Define the profile edgewise, prove its unique finite saturation, and establish unrestricted transfer on the published DMG class to derive union closure, simultaneous admissible-edge saturation, and recovery, all including directed and bidirected loops.

body.related_work: Manten et al. (2025) define the finite directed mixed setting used here, including unordered bidirected pairs with coincident endpoints, prove the directed greatest theorem, give restricted mixed replacements, and state the all-DMG conjecture resolved by Theorem 2. The fixed-profile proposition isolates their replacement regime through the exact tuple consisting of the directed SCC partition, incoming-to-SCC support, occupied cross-SCC bidirected support, exact internal bidirected support including loops, and singleton-SCC directed-loop support. Mogensen and Hansen (2020) supply the closest \(\mu\)-walk proof architecture, not an E-result. Zhang and Spirtes (2005) inform local-change induction under ancestral restrictions. Mooij and Claassen (2020) recover \(\sigma\)-features rather than an E-greatest graph. Claassen and Mooij (2023) treat cyclic directed \(d\)-equivalence. Kook and Mogensen (2026) give optimization encodings without E-union closure. Meek and Sadeghi (2026) give a canonical projection for a different vertex-separation model.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The completed five-vertex falsification gate exhausted \(384{,}168\) bases with at most five edges in the \(35\)-edge subuniverse that excludes bidirected loops. It performed \(12{,}360{,}756\) signature checks, found \(708{,}990\) safe additions and \(254{,}865\) signatures, merged \(94{,}838\) equal-signature collisions, and found no simultaneous or class-union failure. The full five-vertex universe has \(40\) possible edges and \(\sum_{k=0}^{5}\binom{40}{k}=760{,}099\) such sparse bases, so the existing computation does not test bidirected-loop additions and is not the full loop-inclusive early kill gate. All computation is evidence, not a finite obstruction bound or proof.
body.honest_scope: Contextual replacement and unrestricted transfer remain open on the full finite-DMG class, including bidirected loops. Composition, antitonicity, well-defined profile saturation, and fixed-profile E-equivalence are supporting claims. The existing exhaustive sparse check omits bidirected loops. Recovery assumes an exact oracle and makes no faithfulness or finite-sample claim. When all bidirected edges, including bidirected loops, are absent, the result must reduce exactly to Manten et al.'s directed theorem.
